messages:
elena: Dropping an RFC update — proposal now uses capability bits (e.g. `cap_export_reports`) instead of role-name checks in the console. Need quick thumbsup on audit implications.
bryan: Looks good. Two questions: migration ordering and telemetry schema. We must ensure past exports retain kms metadata after mapping.
tess: Agree on capability bits. For UI, don't flip visibility until backend enforces capability. We burned a support incident last year because UI and API diverged.
rachit: On KMS audit: I scanned logs and found ~18 export events where `kms_key_id` is blank. I exported a small sample: `event_id: 2024-09-07-23xx, user: svc-legacy-agent, object: project-42/export-20240907.csv`. Likely from pre-agent-2.0 uploads.
elena: Good find. Migration plan: 1) run dry-run remap to capabilities, 2) for items with missing kms metadata mark them as "legacy_opaque" and require rewrap before allowing export capability.
bryan: For remediation, we should queue a re-wrap workflow that: fetch object -> encrypt with current KMS -> replace object metadata, emit audit entry. We must avoid double-download for large blobs; maybe server-side copy + re-encrypt via storage provider.
tess: Also implement runtime guard: server denies export unless `cap_export_reports` true AND if object.meta.kms_key_id != null OR object.meta.legacy_opaque == false. That prevents leaks while we rewrap.
rachit: Suggest adding a telemetry field `rbac_migration_phase` and `kms_present` to exports so we can chart attempts. Example event: {"kind":"export_attempt","user":"elena","cap":true,"kms_present":false} in logs.
infra-bot: migration-preview job #MP-888 queued. Output: /var/logs/rbac-migration/preview-4861129999.csv (contains dry-run mapping & counts).
security-bot: [NOTICE] Ticket ENGSEC-2026-073 created: RBAC rollout - export capability gating & KMS legacy rewrap. Severity: MED. Assignees: tess, rachit.
bryan: During rollout, implement short cooldown: if a role->capability change happened < 2h ago, deny exports for that actor. Short window prevents rename exploits but keeps admin flexibility. We'll monitor noise.
tess: If we get too many false blocks, we can replace cooldown with requirement: role-change audit entry must include reason tag and owner email. That's heavier but more explicit.
elena: Action items: Elena -> PR to server that enforces `cap_export_reports` + kms checks; Bryan -> rewrap job design + cost estimate; Rachit -> run migration-preview and share CSV; Tess -> add integration tests for rename/rename-exploit and UI gating.
rachit: I'll also add a smoke test that simulates legacy-agent export attempts; expect 403 and audit log entry with `legacy_blocked=true`.
bryan: If we detect ongoing suspicious export attempts during rollout, we should rotate the affected key(s). infra-bot, can you prepare an emergency rotation playbook?
infra-bot: emergency key rotation playbook created: KB-rotate-2026, staging drill scheduled.
security-bot: [ALERT] Potential regression flag: if migration remap sets `cap_export_reports` for teams with existing SSO automations, confirm SSO bots should not inherit export cap by default.
elena: Good catch. Include bot-exclusion rule in migration: skip service accounts unless explicitly whitelisted.
tess: I'll update the test matrix and add a canary cohort (5% orgs) for 48h. Watch `export_attempt.failure` rate and `legacy_blocked` tag.
bryan: Postmortem owner? I'll co-own with Tess. We should document rollback flag: `rbac_v2_ui=false` and `rbac_v2_api=false` to revert.
elena: Thanks all. I'll link PR and migration-preview CSV when ready. Please escalate any anomalous export telemetry to #incidents immediately.
